  matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing Authority,
  the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”) that are not listed
  on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their name and address as a condition
  to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to address the Council are asked to state their
  name and address. Each speaker will be limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may
  not lend any portion of their speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other
  persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.), the
  Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted agenda but
  may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent meeting. The Council
  may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a body and
  not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any member of the Council
  except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor and/or Chair. Members of the
  Council are under no obligation to respond to questions posed by speakers but may provide brief
  clarifying responses to any comment made or questions posed. The Council may not engage in
  any sort of prolonged discussion or deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on
  matters that are not listed on this agenda.

CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL
OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA APPROVING THE CITY OF EL MONTE
CITY CLERK’S CERTIFICATION OF SUFFICIENCY OF TWO VOTER INITIATIVE
PETITIONS FILED WITH THE CITY OF EL MONTE

IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Approve the attached Resolution approving the City of El Monte City Clerk’s
  certification of sufficiency of two voter initiative petitions filed with the City of El
  Monte; and
  2. Provide direction as it relates to the voter initiative measure “Cannabis Business
  and Revenue Generation Tax”; and
  3. Provide direction as it relates to the voter initiative Commercial Cannabis
  Regulation and Public Safety Measure.”

BACKGROUND

On October 23, 2019, two (2) voter initiative petitions were served upon the City Clerk’s
Office of the City of El Monte (the “City Clerk” of the “City”). The voter initiative petitions
were delivered to the Norwalk office of the Los Angeles County Registrar-
Recorder/County Clerk Office of the County of Los Angeles (“the County”) on October
24, 2019 for signature validation. Per statute the signature validation process must be
completed within 30 days.

On November 21, 2019, the City Clerk received two (2) letters from the County
validating the signatures of the two (2) voter initiative petitions (ATTACHMENT 1). In

  10.1
 HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL
NOVEMBER 22, 2019
PAGE 2

order for a voter initiative petition to be validated, at least ten percent (10%) of the
voters registered in the municipality must sign the petition. For the City of El Monte, the
ten percent (10%) threshold is 3,998 registered voters.

DISCUSSION

Certification of Validation of the Voter Initiative Petitions

By the adoption of the attached Resolution, the City Council is certifying the sufficiency
of the voter initiated petitions which were submitted to the City Clerk and whose
signatures were validated by the County.

In the County’s first letter, it verified completion of the signature verification for the
Cannabis Business and Revenue Generation Tax measure and determined that 5,222
signatures (1,224 more than required) were “found sufficient,” enabling the City Clerk’s
certification of sufficiency.

In its second letter, the County verified the completed the signature verification for
Commercial Cannabis Regulation and Public Safety Measure and determined that
5,320 signatures (1,322 more than required) were “found sufficient,” thereby
substantiating a certification of sufficiency by the City Clerk.

City Council Options in Response to the Voter Initiative Petitions

As it relates to the Cannabis Business and Revenue Generation Tax, the City
Council has the following options by which to respond to the petition given the City
Clerk’s findings of sufficiency:

  •  Elections Code Section 9215 options:
  1. Submit the measure to voters at the next regular election (Nov. 2020);
  2. Submit the measure to voters at a special election held between 88 days
  and 103 days after the order of election; OR
  3. Request a report from staff.
  •  Supplemental options:
  1. Submit City Council-initiated counter tax measure to voters concurrent
  with citizens’ proposed tax measure or at a subsequent election.

As it relates to the Commercial Cannabis Regulation and Public Safety Measure,
the City Council has the following options by which to respond to the petition:

  •  Elections Code Section 9215 options:
  1. Adopt the measure without alteration within 10 days of
  presentation;
 HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL
NOVEMBER 22, 2019
PAGE 3

  2. Submit the measure to voters at the next regular election
  (Nov. 2020);
  3. Submit the measure to voters at a special election held
  between 88 days and 103 days after the order of election;
  OR
  4. Request a report from staff.
  •  Supplemental options:
  1. Submit City Council-initiated regulatory counter measure to
  voters concurrent with citizens’ proposed regulatory measure or
  at a subsequent election.

FISCAL IMPACT/FINANCING

There will be no fiscal impact as a result of this action.

CONCLUSION

Staff recommends that the City Council approve the attached Resolution certifying the
City Clerk’s certification of sufficiency of two voter initiative petitions filed with the City.
Staff seeks direction from the City Council as to the course of action in response to the
submitted voter initiative petitions.
 HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL
NOVEMBER 22, 2019
PAGE 4

Respectfully submitted,

ALMA K. MARTINEZ
City Manager

  WHEREAS, on October 23, 2019, two (2) voter initiative petitions were served
upon the City Clerk’s Office of the City of El Monte (the “City Clerk” of the “City”);

  WHEREAS, each petition is on file with the City Clerk;

  WHEREAS, the voter initiative petitions were delivered to the Norwalk office of
the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk Office of the County of Los
Angeles (“the County”) on October 24, 2019 for signature validation

  WHEREAS, the California Elections Code Section 9211 requires the signature
validation process to be completed within 30 days;

  WHEREAS, in order for a voter initiative petition to be validated, at least ten
percent (10%) of the voters registered in the municipality must sign the petition. For the
City, the ten percent (10%) threshold is 3,998 registered voters;

  WHEREAS, in the County’s first letter (Exhibit “A”), it verified completion of the
signature verification for the Cannabis Business and Revenue Generation Tax measure
and determined that 5,222 signatures (1,224 more than required) were “found
sufficient,” enabling the City Clerk’s certification of sufficiency;

  WHEREAS, in its second letter (Exhibit “B”), the County verified the completed
the signature verification for Commercial Cannabis Regulation and Public Safety
Measure and determined that 5,320 signatures (1,322 more than required) were “found
sufficient,” thereby substantiating a certification of sufficiency by the City Clerk.

  WHEREAS, California Elections Code Section 9115(f) requires the City Clerk to
certify the results of the petition examination for sufficiency with the City Council;

  WHEREAS, the City Council seeks to approve the City Clerk’s finding of
sufficiency of the two submitted voter initiative petitions.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA, DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE AND RESOLVE
AS FOLLOWS:

at the November 25, 2019 meeting at which this Resolution was adopted and as stated

and incorporated into the body of this Resolution by this reference.
  SECTION 2. Certification of Sufficiency of Initiative Petitions. The City Council
hereby approves the City Clerk’s certification of sufficiency for the Cannabis Business
and Revenue Generation Tax Measure and the Commercial Cannabis Regulation and
Public Safety Measure, in accordance with the County signature verification letters
attached hereto.
  SECTION 3. This Resolution shall take effect immediately upon its adoption by
the City Council and the City Clerk shall certify to the passage and adoption of this
Resolution and enter it into the book of original Resolutions. The City Council is directed
to take action in accordance with California Elections Code Section 9215.
